title: A Cutting-Edge Parallel Solver for Scalable Power Grid Analysis Using Nested Domain Decomposition
problem: Modern power distribution networks at sub-5nm nodes contain billions to trillions of nodes with reduced noise margins and high power density, creating massive sparse linear systems that conventional domain decomposition methods cannot solve efficiently due to exponentially growing dense Schur complements.
motivation: Accurate and efficient PDN analysis is critical for advanced IC design, but traditional methods face computational bottlenecks as partition counts increase due to dense global Schur complement growth.
method: Proposes nested domain decomposition solver incorporating parallel Schur complement computation strategy and intermediate Schur complement to reduce the size of the final global Schur complement. The intermediate complement breaks the computation into manageable stages.
key_novelty: Introduction of intermediate Schur complement in nested domain decomposition to reduce global Schur complement size and improve parallel scalability.
contributions: Parallel Schur complement computation strategy for hierarchical decomposition
Intermediate Schur complement formulation reducing final global complement size
1.70x speedup in Schur complement computation vs. conventional DDM
1.30x overall solver speedup enabling analysis of massive PDNs
primary_theme: Nested domain decomposition for scalable power grid analysis
